assertion: Baseline Prevotella abundance predicts weight loss in response to a high-fiber/whole grain diet. In a 6-week RCT (n=75 overweight adults), high-Prevotella subjects lost nearly 2 kg more on a whole grain diet compared to refined wheat, while low-Prevotella subjects remained weight-stable. Participants with no detectable Prevotella (0-P group) gained weight on refined wheat but lost weight on whole grain (P=0.009), and showed greater waist circumference reduction (−4.7 vs +0.8 cm, P<0.05).

qualifiers.magnitude: high-P: ~2 kg greater weight loss on WG vs RW; 0-P: 1 kg loss on WG (P=0.009) vs 0.63 kg gain on RW; waist circumference: −4.7 vs +0.8 cm (P<0.05) in low-P group
qualifiers.conditions: ad libitum whole grain wheat/rye products replacing refined wheat for 6 weeks
qualifiers.model: human RCT (3-arm: WG wheat, WG rye, refined wheat)

provenance.ref: ASN Prevotella abundance and weight loss
provenance.original_text: High-P subjects lost nearly 2 kg more on the WG diet when compared with RG, whereas low-P subjects remained weight-stable. 0-P participants experienced a 1 kg loss in body weight with WG consumption (P = 0.009).
